trial_name: CLOVERS — Early Restrictive or Liberal Fluid Management for Sepsis-Induced Hypotension (2023)
citation: Shapiro NI, Douglas IS, Brower RG, Brown SM, Exline MC, Ginde AA, et al. Early restrictive or liberal fluid management for sepsis-induced hypotension. N Engl J Med. 2023;388:499-510.
trial_type: Multicentre, randomised, open-label, pragmatic superiority trial
one_liner: In adults with sepsis-induced hypotension after initial 1–3 L fluid resuscitation, an early restrictive strategy with earlier vasopressors did not significantly alter 90-day mortality compared with a liberal fluid strategy.

pico.population: Adults (≥18 years) with suspected/confirmed infection and sepsis-induced hypotension (SBP <100 mmHg, MAP <65 mmHg, or on vasopressors) after receiving 1–3 L IV crystalloid.
pico.intervention: Early restrictive fluid strategy: prioritised earlier vasopressors (typically norepinephrine targeting MAP ≥65 mmHg) with minimal additional crystalloid during a 24-hour period.
pico.comparison: Early liberal fluid strategy: prioritised additional crystalloid boluses before vasopressors during the 24-hour period.
pico.outcome: Primary outcome: death before discharge home by day 90.

background.existing_knowledge: Sepsis guidelines historically promoted early IV crystalloids (30 mL/kg within first hours) despite low-certainty evidence and risk of fluid accumulation and organ edema.
background.knowledge_gap: Whether to continue fluids versus initiate vasopressors after initial 1–3 L resuscitation in sepsis-induced hypotension remained unresolved by existing trials.
background.hypothesis: An early restrictive fluid strategy prioritising earlier vasopressors improves 90-day outcomes compared with an early liberal fluid strategy.

methods.design: Multicentre, randomised, open-label, pragmatic superiority trial across 60 US centres; allocation stratified by site.
methods.setting: 60 US centers (ED predominant: 93.2% restrictive vs 90.7% liberal; ICU/ward permitted); randomised within 4 hours of eligibility (median 61 minutes).

inclusion: Adults ≥18 years with suspected or confirmed infection
Sepsis-induced hypotension (SBP <100 mmHg or MAP <65 mmHg or receiving vasopressor infusion) after 1–3 L IV isotonic crystalloid
Randomisation within 4 hours of meeting eligibility criteria
exclusion: Clinician-determined need for immediate alternative management pathway
Clinical states where protocolised liberal fluids or fluid restriction would be unsafe (e.g., overt pulmonary oedema / severe volume overload)

methods.intervention: Restrictive strategy: prioritised earlier vasopressors (typically norepinephrine to target MAP ≥65 mmHg) with minimal additional crystalloid for 24 hours. Additional fluid boluses discouraged, permitted only as rescue for severe hypotension or unresponsiveness. Peripheral vasopressors permitted.
methods.comparison: Liberal strategy: prioritised additional isotonic crystalloid boluses early in 24-hour period; vasopressors reserved for persistent hypotension or fluid overload concerns. (Protocol amended during trial making second litre optional; epoch interaction P=0.855).
methods.sample_size_power: Planned 2320 participants for 90% power to detect a 4.5% absolute reduction in 90-day mortality (15.0% to 10.5%, two-sided alpha 0.05). Stopped early for futility at 1563 participants.
methods.primary_outcome: Death before discharge home by day 90.
secondary_outcomes: Death from any cause at any location by day 90
Initiation of mechanical ventilation by day 28
Initiation of renal-replacement therapy by day 28
methods.follow_up: Primary endpoint through day 90; organ support-free days to day 28; organ dysfunction metrics at 72 hours; complications to day 7.

headline_bullets: Stopped early for futility after 2nd interim analysis with 1563 of planned 2320 participants enrolled.
No difference in primary endpoint of death before discharge home by day 90 (13.9% restrictive vs 14.9% liberal; RD −0.9 pp; 95% CI −4.4 to 2.6; P=0.61).
Substantial separation in fluids and vasopressors: median 24-hour total crystalloid 3300 mL vs 5400 mL (difference −2134 mL); vasopressor use 59% vs 37%.

outcomes_table.outcome: Death before discharge home by day 90 (primary)
Death from any cause at any location by day 90
Initiation of mechanical ventilation by day 28
Initiation of renal-replacement therapy by day 28

safety: Serious adverse events occurred in 21 events (restrictive) vs 19 events (liberal) (difference 2 events, 95% CI −10 to 14).
Specific SAE of fluid overload/pulmonary oedema occurred in 0 events (restrictive) vs 3 events (liberal).

domains.notes: Centralised randomisation stratified by institution with concealed allocation before assignment.
Open-label delivery; primary mortality outcome is objective, but secondary endpoints (ICU/hospital-free days) could be susceptible to performance bias.
Intention-to-treat analysis across all 1563 randomised patients (782 restrictive, 781 liberal); censoring rare (0.6% vs 0.5%).

Assigned protocol guidance used in 97.3% (761/782) restrictive vs 96.0% (750/781) liberal. First 6-hour median fluid: 500 mL (IQR 0–1000) vs 2300 mL (IQR 1600–3000); 24-hour total fluid: 3300 mL (IQR 2550–4350) vs 5400 mL (IQR 4400–6575), difference −2134 mL (95% CI −2318 to −1949). Vasopressor use: 59% vs 37%; initiation time 2.4h vs 3.9h (diff −1.4h, 95% CI −1.8 to −1.1); duration 14.4h vs 10.2h (diff 4.2h, 95% CI 2.5 to 5.9). CVC insertion: 42.7% vs 33.6% (diff 9.1 pp, 95% CI 4.4 to 13.8); peripheral vasopressor: 36.9% vs 27.4% (diff 9.5 pp, 95% CI 5.0 to 14.0).
Well-balanced groups: mean age ~62 years, median pre-randomisation crystalloid 2050 mL, mean lactate 2.9 mmol/L, ED enrolment 93.2% vs 90.7%.

internal_validity.verdict: Internal validity is moderate-to-strong with robust randomisation and clear separation, limited by open-label design on secondary outcomes and reduced power from early futility stopping.

domains.notes: Enrolled emergency care sepsis-induced hypotension after median 2050 mL crystalloid with moderate severity (mean lactate 2.9 mmol/L).
Conducted in 60 US centres; highly applicable to ED/early ICU settings in high-income systems, but excludes patients with >3 L fluid pre-enrolment or overt volume overload.

external_validity.verdict: Highly generalisable to high-income emergency and early critical care settings, but less applicable to extreme shock phenotypes or low-resource contexts.

strengths: Large pragmatic multicentre design across 60 US centres
Early randomisation targeting the active clinical decision window (median 61 minutes post-eligibility)
Substantial achieved physiological separation (−2134 mL 24-hr fluid difference, 59% vs 37% vasopressor use)
Objective mortality endpoints evaluated at 90 days
limitations: Open-label design carries risk of performance bias for care-utilization outcomes
Early stopping for futility reduced precision for detecting smaller absolute differences
Intervention bundled multiple actions (fluid limits, vasopressor timing, line placement)
Protocol amendment in liberal group made second fluid litre optional

critical_appraisal.summary: High-quality pragmatic RCT demonstrating that early fluid restriction with vasopressors provides equivalent 90-day survival to liberal fluid resuscitation after initial 1–3 L crystalloid.
strengths: High protocol adherence and marked separation in fluid/vasopressor administration
Pragmatic ED-focused design with objective 90-day mortality outcomes
weaknesses: Stopped early for futility, reducing statistical power

sections.authors_conclusion: An early restrictive fluid strategy did not result in significantly lower or higher 90-day mortality than a liberal fluid strategy among patients with sepsis-induced hypotension.

clinical_bottom_line.verdict: An early vasopressor-prioritised, fluid-restrictive strategy after initial 1–3 L crystalloid is a safe, acceptable alternative to continued liberal fluids, but does not improve survival.
clinical_bottom_line.applies_to: Adults with sepsis-induced hypotension in ED or early ICU settings who have received 1–3 L initial crystalloid.
clinical_bottom_line.does_not_mean: Does not mean initial fluid resuscitation (the first 1–3 L) should be omitted or that fluid administration is harmful.
implementation_caveats: Restrictive fluid strategy increases vasopressor exposure (59% vs 37%) and invasive line insertions (42.7% vs 33.6% CVC rate).
Requires protocolised capability for peripheral vasopressor administration (used in 36.9% vs 27.4%).

controversies.notes: Death before discharge home by day 90 includes social and health-system factors, but all-cause 90-day mortality at any location confirmed neutral result (22.4% vs 21.9%).
Stopped at 1563/2320 patients; primary endpoint CI (-4.4 to 2.6 pp) leaves minor residual uncertainty regarding small benefit or harm.
Second litre was made optional during trial; epoch-by-treatment interaction test showed no differential mortality effect (P=0.855).

context_related_trials.relation: Tested ICU-phase fluid restriction in septic shock and similarly showed no mortality benefit.
Evaluated physiological fluid responsiveness-guided resuscitation in septic shock.
Tested peripheral perfusion-targeted resuscitation versus lactate-targeted resuscitation.

unresolved_questions: Does a specific physiological phenotype (e.g., poor cardiac reserve or severe AKI) benefit from a restrictive fluid strategy?
What is the optimal threshold of initial fluid resuscitation (<1 L vs 1–3 L) before initiating vasopressors?

numbers_to_remember: Stopped early for futility at n=1563
quick_recall.one_line_takeaway: After initial 1–3 L crystalloid, restricting further fluids and using early vasopressors yields identical 90-day outcomes to liberal fluid resuscitation.
